# ActiveCampaign Review 2026: Is This AI-Powered Marketing Automation Worth $15/Month?

## Quick Answer

ActiveCampaign is the best marketing automation platform for businesses that want AI to handle the heavy lifting — and we're not exaggerating. At just $15/month for the Starter plan (1,000 contacts), you get Active Intelligence 2.8, an AI engine that remembers your brand voice, learns from your top-performing campaigns, and generates complete email sequences from a single prompt. The platform saves users an average of 10 hours per week on marketing busywork, delivers a 94.2% email deliverability rate (the highest in the industry), and holds the #1 spot on G2 with over 14,500 reviews and a 4.5/5 average rating. If you want automated email, SMS, and WhatsApp marketing backed by a 30-day money-back guarantee and a CRM that actually works with your existing tools, ActiveCampaign is the answer. The Pro plan at $79/month is the sweet spot — it unlocks full Active Intelligence, predictive sending, and attribution tracking that competitors like Mailchimp and ConvertKit simply don't offer at this price.

## Pros and Cons

### Pros

- **Active Intelligence 2.8 is genuinely useful** — not just another AI gimmick. It remembers your brand voice (Memory), follows your rules automatically (Custom Instructions), and generates entire campaigns from your best-performing emails (Campaign Reference)
- **Industry-leading deliverability at 94.2%** — when your emails land in inboxes instead of spam folders, every other metric improves
- **True multi-channel automation** — email, SMS, and WhatsApp all from one platform with shared automation logic. No need to stitch together separate tools
- **30% recurring affiliate commission** for partners — one of the most generous programs in SaaS, averaging $1,350 per referral with up to 12 months of commissions
- **1,000+ native integrations** cover the full marketing stack: Shopify, WooCommerce, Stripe, Salesforce, WordPress, Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram, Calendly, and Zapier
- **Free migration from any competitor** — ActiveCampaign's team will move your contacts, automations, and templates at no cost
- **14-day free trial + 30-day money-back guarantee** — you can test the full platform for two weeks without a credit card, and if you commit to a paid plan and don't see results in 30 days, they'll refund you
- **AI-powered predictive sending** — the platform analyzes individual contact behavior to determine the optimal send time for each person, boosting open rates without manual A/B testing

### Cons

- **Starter plan is extremely limited** — only 5 actions per automation and limited segmentation make it feel more like a demo than a usable tool. You need Plus ($49/month) to do real marketing automation
- **Learning curve at the Pro level** — the visual automation builder is powerful but complex. Users migrating from simpler tools like Mailchimp will need 2-4 weeks to feel comfortable with conditional logic and split automation paths
- **Active Intelligence limited on lower tiers** — the AI features that make ActiveCampaign special (Memory, Campaign Reference, Custom Instructions) are either limited or unavailable on Starter and Plus plans
- **WhatsApp and SMS cost extra** — while the Email plan includes core features, adding WhatsApp or SMS channels requires separate plans or add-ons that increase the monthly cost
- **CRM requires add-ons for full functionality** — Pipelines and sales engagement features are paid add-ons, not included in the base CRM

## Who Is ActiveCampaign For?

ActiveCampaign is ideal for:

- **Small to mid-sized businesses** (1-50 employees) that want to automate their marketing without a dedicated marketing operations team
- **E-commerce stores** using Shopify, WooCommerce, or BigCommerce — the deep e-commerce integrations trigger automations based on purchase behavior, abandoned carts, and product views
- **Agencies and consultants** managing multiple clients — the agency partner program includes white-label options, client-specific AI agents, and a unified dashboard for managing thousands of contacts across accounts
- **Content creators and course sellers** who need advanced tagging, lead scoring, and conditional content to nurture subscribers through multi-step funnels
- **B2B companies** that need CRM + marketing automation in one platform — the built-in CRM with lead scoring replaces the need for separate tools like HubSpot for smaller teams

ActiveCampaign is NOT ideal for:

- **Absolute beginners** who just want to send a monthly newsletter — Mailchimp's free plan or Kit (ConvertKit) are simpler starting points
- **Enterprise teams with 100+ users** — the user limits (1-5 users per plan) require Enterprise for larger teams, which starts at $145/month and scales up
- **Companies that only need transactional emails** — ActiveCampaign's strength is in marketing automation, not transactional email delivery (use SendGrid or Postmark for that)

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### Active Intelligence 2.8 — AI That Actually Does the Work

ActiveCampaign's AI, called Active Intelligence 2.8, is the platform's crown jewel and what separates it from every other email marketing tool on the market. Unlike basic AI assistants that just rewrite subject lines, Active Intelligence is a multi-component AI system designed to automate the entire campaign creation process.

**Memory** is the feature that changes everything. It remembers every detail of your brand — your voice, your audience's preferences, what worked in past campaigns — and applies that knowledge to every new campaign without you having to re-explain yourself. Each interaction builds on the last. If you launch a welcome sequence that gets high engagement, Memory learns from it and applies those patterns to your next campaign.

**Custom Instructions** let you set your brand rules once. Tone of voice, industry terminology to use or avoid, compliance requirements, formatting preferences — define them once and every AI-generated campaign follows them automatically. This matters because it solves the biggest problem with AI-generated marketing: inconsistency. Without Custom Instructions, AI assistants produce content that sounds generic. With them, every email sounds like your brand wrote it.

**Brand Kit** extends this to visual consistency. Your logo, colors, fonts, and imagery are stored in the system. When Active Intelligence generates a campaign, it pulls from your brand kit to ensure every email looks unmistakably yours. No more emails that look like they came from a different company because someone picked the wrong template.

**Campaign Reference** is perhaps the most practical feature. Instead of starting from a blank page, you can tell Active Intelligence to build from your best-performing emails. Select a top campaign, point the AI at it, and it generates variations optimized for different segments, occasions, or goals — all while preserving what made the original work.

In practice, Active Intelligence can generate a complete email campaign from a single prompt. Tell it "create a three-email welcome sequence for new subscribers who signed up through our lead magnet about Facebook ads," and it generates subject lines, body copy, CTAs, and audience segment rules — all in your brand voice, with your brand kit, and optimized based on past performance data.

### Email Marketing — Built for Deliverability

ActiveCampaign's email marketing engine is built around one metric most platforms ignore: deliverability. At 94.2%, ActiveCampaign holds the highest email deliverability rate in the industry, which means your emails actually reach inboxes — not spam folders, not promotions tabs, not the void.

The platform achieves this through a combination of infrastructure quality (dedicated IPs available, strong sender reputation management), smart sending algorithms (predictive sending that sends each email at the optimal time for each individual contact), and automated list hygiene (inactive contact management, bounce handling, and engagement-based segmentation).

Beyond deliverability, the email builder supports drag-and-drop templates, a growing library of AI-generated templates, and a plain-text editor for purists. Personalization goes deep — you can insert not just first names, but any custom field, conditional content blocks that show different text based on contact data, and dynamic product recommendations pulled from your e-commerce store.

A/B testing covers subject lines, content, send times, and sender names. Results aren't just reported — ActiveCampaign can automatically pick the winner and send it to the remaining audience, saving you the manual follow-up step.

### Marketing Automation — The Visual Builder That Scales

ActiveCampaign's visual automation builder is where the platform earned its reputation. It's a node-based canvas where you build automations by connecting triggers, actions, conditions, and goals.

Triggers can be anything: form submissions, page visits, email opens, link clicks, purchase events, tag changes, custom field updates, or API calls from external tools. Actions include sending emails, SMS, WhatsApp messages, adding/removing tags, updating custom fields, creating deals, sending webhooks, and triggering other automations.

The conditional logic is what sets it apart. You can build automations that branch based on almost anything — if a contact opened the email but didn't click, send a follow-up; if they clicked and visited the pricing page but didn't purchase in 48 hours, notify sales; if they purchased, move them to the customer onboarding sequence. This level of branching is possible in tools like HubSpot and Marketo, but usually at much higher price points.

Goals are a unique feature that act as exit conditions for automations. Set a goal like "completed purchase" or "booked demo," and contacts that hit the goal are automatically removed from the automation — no more annoying follow-up emails to people who already converted.

The Starter plan limits you to 5 actions per automation, which quickly becomes restrictive. Plus ($49/month) unlocks unlimited automation actions, which is what you need to build real, multi-step customer journeys.

### CRM — Sales and Marketing in One Place

ActiveCampaign includes a built-in CRM that connects your marketing automations directly to your sales pipeline. This isn't a full-featured sales CRM like Salesforce or HubSpot Sales Hub, but for small to mid-sized teams, it eliminates the need for a separate tool.

Key CRM features include lead scoring (automatically rank contacts based on engagement and behavior), deal tracking with pipeline stages, task management for follow-ups, and contact timelines that show every interaction — emails opened, links clicked, pages visited, forms submitted.

Two paid add-ons extend the CRM's capabilities: **Pipelines** adds visual deal management with drag-and-drop stages, automated deal creation from automations, and revenue reporting. **Sales Engagement** adds email sequences for sales outreach, meeting scheduling, and call tracking — essentially turning ActiveCampaign into a lightweight sales engagement platform.

The CRM integrates bidirectionally with Shopify, WooCommerce, Salesforce, and other major platforms, so contact data flows automatically between systems without manual exports or imports.

### Integrations — 1,000+ Ways to Connect Your Stack

ActiveCampaign's integration ecosystem is one of its strongest selling points. With 1,000+ native integrations, it connects to virtually every tool in the marketing and sales stack:

**E-commerce:** Shopify, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Square, Stripe, PayPal — deep integrations that sync purchase history, trigger abandoned cart automations, and power product recommendations.

**CRM & Sales:** Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho CRM, HubSpot — bidirectional sync keeps sales and marketing aligned.

**Content & Web:** WordPress (with a dedicated plugin), Wix, Squarespace, Webflow, Unbounce, Leadpages — embed forms, trigger automations from page visits, and track conversions.

**Advertising:** Facebook Ads, Google Ads, Instagram — sync audiences between your ad platforms and email lists for retargeting and lookalike audiences.

**Productivity:** Slack, Google Sheets, Calendly, DocuSign, Zoom, Microsoft Teams — automate notifications, schedule follow-ups, and log interactions.

**Payments & Billing:** Stripe, PayPal, QuickBooks, Xero, Chargebee — trigger automations based on subscription events, payment failures, and plan changes.

If a native integration doesn't exist, ActiveCampaign's API and Zapier support fill the gap. The API is well-documented and supports custom integrations for developers.

## Pricing

ActiveCampaign's pricing is based on two factors: the plan tier and the number of contacts. All prices below are for 1,000 contacts, billed annually (monthly billing is available at a higher rate):

| Plan | Monthly Price (1K contacts, annual) | Key Features |
|------|-------------------------------------|--------------|
| **Starter** | $15/month | Email marketing, basic automation (5 actions per automation), limited segmentation, Active Intelligence (limited), 1 user |
| **Plus** | $49/month | Unlimited automation actions, landing pages, standard segmentation, Active Intelligence (limited), 1 user |
| **Pro** | $79/month | Full Active Intelligence, predictive sending, conditional content, attribution tracking, advanced segmentation, 3 users |
| **Enterprise** | $145/month | Premium segmentation, custom objects, SSO, dedicated account team, 5 users, unlimited automation actions |

**What happens as your contact list grows:** The price scales with contact count. At 10,000 contacts, the Plus plan costs approximately $115/month, and Pro costs approximately $170/month. At 25,000 contacts, Plus is around $209/month and Pro is around $279/month. The platform never locks you out or penalizes you for growing — it simply prompts you to upgrade to the next contact band.

**Hidden costs to watch for:**
- **SMS and WhatsApp** — these channels require separate plans or add-ons beyond the Email plan. Pricing depends on message volume and destination country.
- **CRM add-ons** — Pipelines and Sales Engagement are paid add-ons (typically $25-$50/month each), not included in any base plan.
- **Monthly billing surcharge** — annual billing saves 20-25% compared to month-to-month. Starter's $15/month becomes roughly $19/month on monthly billing.

**Breakeven analysis:** If ActiveCampaign saves you 10 hours per week (the average reported by users), and your time is worth $30/hour, that's $300/week or $15,600/year in recovered productivity. At $49/month (Plus plan), your ROI is approximately 32x. Even at the $79/month Pro plan, the breakeven point is roughly 3 hours saved per month — achievable with a single automated welcome sequence.

**Free trial and guarantee:** The 14-day free trial requires no credit card and gives full platform access. If you switch from a competitor, ActiveCampaign's team will migrate your contacts, automations, and templates for free. The 30-day money-back guarantee applies after you start a paid plan — if you don't see results, you get a full refund.

## Buyer's Guide: How to Choose the Right Email Marketing Platform

Choosing an email marketing platform in 2026 isn't just about sending newsletters — it's about finding a system that can grow with your business, automate the repetitive parts of marketing, and integrate with the tools you already use. Here's what to prioritize:

**1. Automation capabilities over email templates.** Pretty templates are nice, but automation is what saves you time and makes you money. Look for visual automation builders that support conditional branching, multi-step sequences, and goal-based exits. If a platform limits you to simple "if this, then that" logic, you'll outgrow it within months.

**2. Deliverability is non-negotiable.** A 5% difference in deliverability can mean thousands of dollars in lost revenue. Check independent deliverability benchmarks (EmailToolTester, Litmus, and G2 reviews are good sources). ActiveCampaign's 94.2% rate is the gold standard — anything below 90% is a red flag.

**3. AI should do the work, not just suggest subject lines.** Most platforms have "AI features" that amount to a subject line generator. That's table stakes in 2026. Look for AI that understands your brand voice, learns from your campaign performance, and can generate complete sequences from a prompt. ActiveCampaign's Memory and Campaign Reference features are examples of what separates real AI from checkbox AI.

**4. Multi-channel is the future.** Email is the foundation, but SMS and WhatsApp are increasingly important channels — especially for e-commerce, appointment reminders, and time-sensitive offers. A platform that handles all three from one automation builder saves you from managing three separate tools.

**5. CRM integration matters more than you think.** If you're a B2B company or sell high-ticket products, having your marketing automation connected to a CRM is essential. It's the difference between sending generic email blasts and triggering personalized outreach based on sales activity.

**6. Pricing should scale with value, not just contacts.** Some platforms charge per contact but give you the same features at every tier. Others gate advanced features behind pricing tiers. ActiveCampaign's approach — feature gates by plan tier, plus contact-based scaling — is pragmatic. Most businesses should start on Plus ($49/month) and upgrade to Pro ($79/month) when they need predictive sending and attribution.

## Competitor Comparisons

### ActiveCampaign vs Mailchimp

Mailchimp is the most recognized name in email marketing, but its positioning has shifted toward a broader marketing platform (including websites, social media scheduling, and ads) — often at the expense of email depth.

**Automation:** ActiveCampaign wins decisively. Mailchimp's automation builder caps at 4 branches and doesn't support the kind of conditional logic ActiveCampaign handles effortlessly. For anything beyond a welcome sequence or abandoned cart, ActiveCampaign is the better tool.

**Pricing:** Mailchimp's free plan (up to 500 contacts) makes it attractive for complete beginners, but costs escalate quickly. At 5,000 contacts, Mailchimp's Standard plan is approximately $100/month vs ActiveCampaign Plus at $70/month — and ActiveCampaign includes more automation features at that price.

**Verdict:** Choose Mailchimp if you're a beginner sending basic newsletters to under 1,000 subscribers. Choose ActiveCampaign if you plan to use automation, segmentation, or sell anything.

### ActiveCampaign vs ConvertKit (Kit)

ConvertKit (now rebranded as Kit) is designed specifically for creators — bloggers, YouTubers, podcasters, and course creators. Its simplicity is its strength and its limitation.

**Automation:** ActiveCampaign's visual builder is significantly more powerful. ConvertKit's automation is linear — do this, then do that. ActiveCampaign supports conditional branching, split testing within automations, and goal-based exits that ConvertKit can't match.

**Pricing:** At 1,000 subscribers, ConvertKit's Creator plan is $25/month vs ActiveCampaign Starter at $15/month. But at 10,000 subscribers, ConvertKit jumps to $99/month vs ActiveCampaign Plus at $115/month. They're comparable at scale, but ActiveCampaign includes a CRM and more advanced features.

**Verdict:** Choose ConvertKit if you're a solo creator who wants simplicity above all else. Choose ActiveCampaign if you want more automation power, CRM features, and room to scale — especially if you sell products or services.

### ActiveCampaign vs HubSpot

HubSpot is the 800-pound gorilla in marketing and sales. Its Marketing Hub is powerful, but the pricing reflects it.

**Features:** HubSpot Marketing Hub Professional starts at $800/month for 1,000 contacts — that's 10x ActiveCampaign's Pro plan. HubSpot offers more advanced analytics, a full-featured CMS, and deeper sales integration, but for pure marketing automation, ActiveCampaign matches or exceeds HubSpot's capabilities at a fraction of the cost.

**CRM:** HubSpot's CRM is free and more feature-rich than ActiveCampaign's built-in CRM. If CRM is your primary need, HubSpot is the better choice. But if you're primarily doing email marketing automation with light CRM needs, ActiveCampaign delivers 80% of the value at 10% of the price.

**Verdict:** Choose HubSpot if you need a full sales + marketing + service suite and have the budget. Choose ActiveCampaign if you want powerful marketing automation without the enterprise price tag.

### ActiveCampaign vs GetResponse

GetResponse is the closest direct competitor to ActiveCampaign in terms of features and pricing.

**AI:** ActiveCampaign's Active Intelligence 2.8 is more advanced than GetResponse's AI features. ActiveCampaign's Memory and Campaign Reference features have no direct equivalent in GetResponse.

**Webinars:** GetResponse includes a built-in webinar platform — something ActiveCampaign doesn't offer. If webinars are central to your marketing, GetResponse has an edge.

**Pricing:** Very similar. At 1,000 contacts, GetResponse's Marketing Automation plan is $59/month vs ActiveCampaign Pro at $79/month. Slight edge to GetResponse on price.

**Verdict:** Choose GetResponse if webinars are essential to your strategy. Otherwise, ActiveCampaign's superior AI, deliverability, and automation builder make it the better choice for most businesses.

## Real-World User Feedback

ActiveCampaign is the #1 rated marketing automation platform on G2, with over 14,500 reviews and a 4.5/5 average score. Here's what real users are saying:

**"People joke when I talk about ActiveCampaign, they say it sounds like I'm a paid spokesperson. I have to tell them no, I actually really believe in it because it has made my life so much easier."** — Palmetto Fortis case study. The agency increased client open rates from 22% to 52% and boosted sales by 20% using ActiveCampaign's intelligent automation and lead scoring.

**On G2, the most praised features** are the visual automation builder (consistently called "best in class"), email deliverability, and the depth of integrations. The most common criticism is the learning curve — users migrating from Mailchimp or basic email tools report 2-4 weeks of adjustment, particularly around the automation builder's advanced features and the difference between lists and tags.

**88% of users say** ActiveCampaign delivers value faster than competitors. This aligns with the platform's "time to first value" metric — the average user sends their first automated campaign within 18 minutes of signing up, and the platform estimates 10 hours saved per week once fully configured.

**ActiveCampaign's Customer Success Commitment** — a set of 17 promises covering uptime, support response times, data security, and migration assistance — is frequently cited as a reason businesses stay long-term. The commitment includes free migration from any competitor, guaranteed 99.9% uptime, and a dedicated onboarding specialist for Pro and Enterprise plans.

## 7 Tips to Get the Most Out of ActiveCampaign

**1. Start with the Plus plan, not Starter.** The 5-action automation limit on Starter will frustrate you within the first week. Plus ($49/month) unlocks unlimited automation actions — you'll build real workflows, not demos. The $34/month difference pays for itself in one automated sequence that would otherwise require manual work.

**2. Set up Active Intelligence Custom Instructions immediately.** Before you send your first campaign, define your brand rules — tone of voice, industry terms to use or avoid, compliance notes, formatting preferences. Every AI-generated campaign after that will follow these rules automatically. This 15-minute investment prevents hours of editing later.

**3. Use goal-based automations instead of time-based sequences.** Instead of "send email 2 three days after email 1," set a goal like "clicked CTA link" as the trigger for the next step. Contacts who convert early skip the remaining follow-ups, and those who need more nurturing get it — automatically. This is the single biggest efficiency gain over tools like Mailchimp.

**4. Tag strategically, don't create lists.** ActiveCampaign uses a tag-based system, not list-based. A contact can have multiple tags (e.g., "lead-magnet-A," "visited-pricing," "customer") while existing in a single account. This prevents duplicate contacts and makes segmentation far more flexible than traditional list-based platforms.

**5. Connect your e-commerce store on day one.** If you use Shopify, WooCommerce, or similar, integrate it immediately — not after you've "figured out" the platform. The deep e-commerce integrations unlock abandoned cart recovery, post-purchase sequences, and product recommendation automations that directly generate revenue. These automations alone typically cover the monthly subscription cost.

**6. Use the free migration service if you're switching.** ActiveCampaign's team will move your contacts, automations, and templates from your current platform at no cost. This isn't just a CSV import — they'll map your existing automations to ActiveCampaign's builder, preserving your workflows. It saves 10-20 hours of manual migration work.

**7. Review the automation reports weekly, not monthly.** ActiveCampaign's automation reporting shows where contacts enter, exit, and get stuck in your workflows. A weekly 10-minute review catches broken automations, identifies underperforming emails, and surfaces conversion bottlenecks before they cost you a month of lost revenue.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Is ActiveCampaign better than Mailchimp?

Yes — for anyone doing more than basic newsletter sends. ActiveCampaign's automation builder, CRM integration, and AI features far exceed Mailchimp's capabilities. Mailchimp is simpler and has a free plan for up to 500 contacts, which makes it a good starting point. But once you need multi-step automations, conditional logic, or CRM functionality, ActiveCampaign is the clear winner. At comparable contact counts, ActiveCampaign is also usually cheaper than Mailchimp's paid plans.

### How much does ActiveCampaign really cost?

For 1,000 contacts billed annually, the plans are: Starter $15/month, Plus $49/month, Pro $79/month, and Enterprise $145/month. The Plus plan is the realistic starting point for most businesses since Starter's 5-action automation limit is restrictive. Prices increase with contact count — at 10,000 contacts, Plus costs approximately $115/month and Pro costs $170/month.

### Does ActiveCampaign have a free plan?

No, ActiveCampaign does not offer a permanent free plan. It offers a 14-day free trial with full platform access and no credit card required. After the trial, you need a paid plan. However, the trial is generous — you can build and launch real automations, not just test with dummy data.

### What is Active Intelligence and do I need it?

Active Intelligence 2.8 is ActiveCampaign's AI engine. It includes Memory (remembers your brand and past campaigns), Custom Instructions (follows your brand rules automatically), Brand Kit (maintains visual consistency), and Campaign Reference (builds from your best-performing emails). You don't strictly "need" it to use ActiveCampaign, but it's what separates the platform from competitors. On Starter and Plus plans, Active Intelligence has usage limits. Full access comes with the Pro plan.

### How does ActiveCampaign compare to HubSpot?

ActiveCampaign is better for pure marketing automation at a small-to-mid-market price point. HubSpot Marketing Hub offers deeper analytics, a built-in CMS, and tighter sales integration — but starts at $800/month for comparable features. ActiveCampaign at $79/month (Pro) delivers 80% of HubSpot's marketing automation capabilities at 10% of the cost. If CRM is your primary need, HubSpot's free CRM is superior. If marketing automation is the focus, ActiveCampaign wins on value.

### Can I send SMS and WhatsApp messages from ActiveCampaign?

Yes, but these channels require separate plans or add-ons beyond the standard Email plan. SMS and WhatsApp automation are available and integrate with the same visual automation builder you use for email. Pricing depends on message volume and destination country. For businesses that primarily need email marketing, the base plan is sufficient.

### Is ActiveCampaign good for e-commerce?

Yes — it's one of the best platforms for e-commerce. The deep integrations with Shopify, WooCommerce, and BigCommerce enable abandoned cart recovery, post-purchase follow-ups, product recommendations, and win-back campaigns based on actual purchase behavior. The predictive sending feature optimizes send times for each customer based on when they're most likely to open and engage.

### How long does it take to learn ActiveCampaign?

Plan on 2-4 weeks to feel comfortable if you're migrating from a simpler tool like Mailchimp. The email builder and basic automations are learnable in a few days. The visual automation builder with conditional logic takes longer — expect to spend the first week building simple sequences, the second week adding conditions and goals, and weeks 3-4 optimizing and connecting automations across your full customer journey. ActiveCampaign's free migration service and onboarding specialists (Pro plan and above) accelerate this significantly.

### Does ActiveCampaign offer phone support?

ActiveCampaign primarily provides support through chat and ticket systems, with phone support available on Enterprise plans. All plans include access to the knowledge base, video tutorials, and ActiveTraining resources. The Customer Success Commitment guarantees response times and support quality across all plans.

### What happens when I exceed my contact limit?

ActiveCampaign doesn't penalize you or lock features when you exceed your plan's contact limit. The platform simply prompts you to upgrade to the next contact band. You keep all your data, automations, and functionality — you just need to move to the appropriate pricing tier for your list size. This is more generous than some competitors who restrict features or charge overage fees.

## Conclusion

ActiveCampaign is the most complete AI-powered marketing automation platform you can buy for under $100/month — and we've reviewed dozens of alternatives. The combination of Active Intelligence 2.8 (which genuinely automates campaign creation, not just subject lines), industry-leading email deliverability (94.2%), a visual automation builder that supports complex conditional logic, and 1,000+ integrations makes it the best choice for businesses that want to do more than send newsletters.

The platform isn't perfect — the Starter plan's limitations feel punitive, the learning curve at Pro level is real, and SMS/WhatsApp channels cost extra. But these are reasonable trade-offs for a tool that saves users an average of 10 hours per week and delivers measurable ROI from the first month.

**Our recommendation:** Start with the 14-day free trial on the Plus plan. Build a welcome sequence, connect your e-commerce store or website, and set up Active Intelligence Custom Instructions. If you like what you see (and we're confident you will), upgrade to Pro ($79/month) to unlock predictive sending, attribution tracking, and full Active Intelligence. The 30-day money-back guarantee means there's no risk — if it doesn't deliver results, you get your money back.
